1.1 Document Information
1.2 Ground-Truth Statement
This document is completely synthetic and self-contained. It is the only source of truth
for the Vehicle Gateway Control System. Any fact that is not stated in this document is
not specified in this HLD.
The Vehicle Gateway Control System contains exactly five primary Software
Components, exactly three primary Interfaces, exactly five explicit Signals, and exactly
six Port mappings.

2. System Architecture
2.1 System Overview
The Vehicle Gateway Control System is composed of exactly five primary Software
Components:
1. SensorInterface
2. VehicleControlComponent
3. BrakeControlComponent
4. DiagnosticManager
5. CommunicationManager
No other Software Components are defined in this HLD.
The system has two functional flows:

The primary control flow carries VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed, and BrakeStatus from
SensorInterface through VehicleControlComponent to BrakeControlComponent.
The diagnostic flow carries DiagnosticRequest and DiagnosticResponse between
CommunicationManager and DiagnosticManager.
2.2 Software Component Responsibilities
2.2.1 SensorInterface
SensorInterface is responsible for acquiring and normalizing physical vehicle sensor
information. SensorInterface provides VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed.
2.2.2 VehicleControlComponent
VehicleControlComponent processes vehicle-speed and engine-speed information and
generates brake control status. VehicleControlComponent consumes VehicleSpeed and
EngineSpeed. VehicleControlComponent provides BrakeStatus.
2.2.3 BrakeControlComponent
BrakeControlComponent consumes brake-related control and status information for
vehicle deceleration actuation. BrakeControlComponent consumes BrakeStatus.
2.2.4 DiagnosticManager
DiagnosticManager processes diagnostic requests and generates diagnostic responses.
DiagnosticManager consumes DiagnosticRequest. DiagnosticManager provides
DiagnosticResponse.
2.2.5 CommunicationManager
CommunicationManager provides communication transport services for CAN and
Automotive Ethernet. CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to
DiagnosticManager. CommunicationManager consumes DiagnosticResponse.

3.4 Port Connections
VehicleDataOut of SensorInterface is connected to VehicleDataIn of
VehicleControlComponent through VehicleDataInterface.
BrakeStatusOut of VehicleControlComponent is connected to BrakeStatusIn of
BrakeControlComponent through BrakeStatusInterface.
DiagnosticOut of DiagnosticManager is connected to DiagnosticIn of
CommunicationManager through DiagnosticInterface.
The HLD defines no additional port for DiagnosticRequest. The six ports in Section 3.2 are
the complete port set.
4. Interfaces and Signals
4.1 Interface Definitions
The Vehicle Gateway Control System defines exactly three primary Interfaces.
4.1.1 VehicleDataInterface
VehicleDataInterface uses the Sender-Receiver communication pattern.
VehicleDataInterface contains the signals VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed. VehicleSpeed
is contained in VehicleDataInterface. EngineSpeed is contained in VehicleDataInterface.
4.1.2 BrakeStatusInterface
BrakeStatusInterface uses the Sender-Receiver communication pattern.
BrakeStatusInterface contains the signal BrakeStatus.

5. Communication Architecture
5.1 Primary Protocol: Controller Area Network (CAN)
Controller Area Network (CAN) is the primary communication protocol of the Vehicle
Gateway Control System. CAN is the primary communication protocol for all five explicit

VehicleSpeed
EngineSpeed
BrakeStatus

CAN is the primary transport mechanism for VehicleSpeed. CAN is the primary transport
mechanism for EngineSpeed. CAN is the primary transport mechanism for BrakeStatus.
CAN is the primary transport mechanism for DiagnosticRequest. CAN is the primary
transport mechanism for DiagnosticResponse.

6. End-to-End Data Flows and Dependency Summary
6.1 Primary Control Data Flow
The primary control flow is:
SensorInterface → VehicleSpeed / EngineSpeed → VehicleControlComponent →
BrakeStatus → BrakeControlComponent
1. SensorInterface acquires and normalizes vehicle sensor information.
2. SensorInterface provides VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed to
VehicleControlComponent through VehicleDataInterface.
3. VehicleControlComponent consumes VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed.
4. VehicleControlComponent calculates vehicle control state.
5. VehicleControlComponent provides BrakeStatus to BrakeControlComponent through
BrakeStatusInterface.
6. BrakeControlComponent consumes BrakeStatus for vehicle deceleration actuation.
CAN is the primary communication protocol for VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed, and
BrakeStatus.
6.2 Diagnostic Data Flow
The diagnostic flow is:
CommunicationManager → DiagnosticRequest → DiagnosticManager →
DiagnosticResponse → CommunicationManager
1. CommunicationManager receives an external diagnostic request.
2. CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to DiagnosticManager through
DiagnosticInterface.
3. DiagnosticManager processes the request.
4. DiagnosticManager provides DiagnosticResponse to CommunicationManager through
DiagnosticInterface.
5. CommunicationManager consumes DiagnosticResponse and performs transport of
the response.
CAN is the primary communication protocol for DiagnosticRequest and
DiagnosticResponse.

7. Diagnostic Architecture and Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundary
This section is the authoritative source for diagnostic scope boundaries in VH-GW-
HLD-002.
7.1 Diagnostic Architecture
The diagnostic architecture uses two Software Components:
DiagnosticManager processes diagnostic requests and generates diagnostic
responses.
CommunicationManager receives external diagnostic requests and transports
diagnostic responses.
The two Software Components communicate through DiagnosticInterface.
DiagnosticInterface uses a Client-Server / Sender-Receiver hybrid communication
pattern and contains DiagnosticRequest and DiagnosticResponse.
CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to DiagnosticManager.
DiagnosticManager provides DiagnosticResponse to CommunicationManager.
No additional diagnostic components are defined in this HLD.
7.2 Diagnostic Protocol and Transport
The HLD specifies:
UDS over CAN
